definition: The Ho–Kashyap algorithm is an iterative method in machine learning for finding a linear decision boundary that separates two linearly separable classes.
details: It was developed by Yu-Chi Ho and Rangasami L. Kashyap in 1965, and usually presented as a problem in linear programming.

explainer.lead: The Ho–Kashyap algorithm is an iterative method for finding a linear decision boundary that separates two linearly separable classes. It matters because it recasts classifier training as a linear programming problem.

tiers.eli5: Imagine nudging a straight line again and again until every dot of one color sits on one side and every dot of the other color on the other. The algorithm repeats small corrections until that line works.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to train linear classifiers when the classes can be cleanly split, iterating to adjust the boundary. A pitfall is that it assumes linear separability, so non-separable data gives no clean solution.
tiers.paperLevel: It iteratively updates a weight vector and margin vector to satisfy a set of linear inequalities separating the classes, usually presented as a linear programming problem. Its scope is limited to linearly separable classes.

explainer.example: Given two clusters of points that a straight line can divide, the algorithm starts from an initial boundary and updates it step by step until all points are correctly separated.
